html:
A long series of armed struggles in Mexico from 1910 to about 1920, often called the defining event of modern Mexican history. It began as a revolt against the dictator Porfirio Díaz and became a civil war among the revolutionaries themselves.

Díaz had ruled for over thirty years. Railways and foreign investment had grown, but most land was in the hands of a few great estates, and peasants and workers had no say. The main stages:

  • 1910 to 1911: Francisco Madero calls for revolt after a rigged election; Díaz goes into exile.
  • 1913: General Victoriano Huerta overthrows and has Madero murdered.
  • 1914: Huerta is driven out; the revolutionaries split. In the north, Pancho Villa; in the south, Emiliano Zapata fights for "land and liberty".
  • 1915 to 1920: Venustiano Carranza and his general Álvaro Obregón win out and pass the Constitution of 1917.

Perhaps a million people or more died, of fighting, hunger and disease, and many fled to the United States. The revolution destroyed the old federal army and led to land reform, workers' rights and limits on the church, which sparked the Cristero War. It also inspired the art of Mexican muralism.
